_comment: Copy this file to server_config.json next to experimentalserver.py and edit it. It is strict JSON, so it cannot hold real comments: every "_comment_*" key below is ignored by the server (it only reads the exact names documented here) and is safe to leave in. Every value the server treats as privileged lives in THIS file or in the two files named at the bottom - none of them is in experimentalserver.py. With this example as-is the server runs fine for local client testing and grants nobody any privilege.
_comment_bind: Which address the HTTP and RTA (websocket) servers listen on. Keep "127.0.0.1" for local testing. "0.0.0.0" exposes it to your whole network; on a public host keep it loopback and put a reverse proxy (Caddy/nginx) in front for HTTPS.
_comment_httpPort: Port for the Xbox Live compatibility HTTP API.
_comment_rtaPort: Port for the RTA websocket (/connect). The game keeps one open for its whole session.
_comment_relayBind: Address the UDP peer relay binds to. It carries dungeon traffic between players and is NOT proxied, so it needs its own open UDP port.
_comment_relayPort: UDP port for the peer relay. Set to 0 to turn the relay off entirely (lobbies still work; players then need to reach each other directly).
_comment_owners: PRIVILEGED ALLOW-LIST. A list of xuidBase strings; any of that player's four XUIDs works. Owners - and only owners - may switch events (/windurango/admin/events*), grant jewels, revoke achievements, publish a client release, set minClientVersion, and see every player on the players/relay/achievements routes. Empty list (the default here) = NOBODY is an owner, which is the safe state. To make yourself an owner on your own test server: start the server, let your game sign in once, find your "xuidBase" in data/_players.json (or in your winDurango.json), and put that number here as a string. Never copy another server's owner list.
_comment_clientUpdateKey: The PUBLIC half of your release-signing RSA key (2048-8192 bit), or a list of them. Used only to VERIFY release.json signatures; the server never signs anything and a private key here is refused. Accepted shapes: .NET <RSAKeyValue>...</RSAKeyValue> (what ReleaseTool.exe prints), PEM/base64 DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo or PKCS#1, or a JWK {"kty":"RSA","n":"...","e":"AQAB"}. Example of the shape (NOT a usable key): "<RSAKeyValue><Modulus>REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_PUBLIC_MODULUS</Modulus><Exponent>AQAB</Exponent></RSAKeyValue>". To make a real one, generate your own RSA keypair with ReleaseTool.exe (or openssl genrsa) and put ONLY the public half here - keep the private half offline, never on the server. Empty (the default) = no client release is served or published, which is fine for client testing.
_comment_minClientVersion: Lock out launchers older than this, e.g. "2026.9.19.1200". Verified players below it get 426 update_required on every route except the client/identity/players ones; owners are never blocked. null (the default) = nobody is blocked. Refused above the published release unless forced, so nobody can be locked out with no way to update.
_comment_peerDirect: Kill switch for direct player-to-player connections. false tells every game at once to use the relay only, and forgets every pair key. Read again while the server runs - no restart.
_comment_peerDirectLan: false leaves LAN and VPN addresses out of the peer lists (players behind one public IP then use the relay too). Read again while the server runs.
_comment_allowRealPeerAddresses: true lets players publish their real IP:port as their secureDeviceAddress instead of their relay address. Only for a trusted LAN/VPN group that does not use the relay - it exposes players' addresses to each other. Leave false unless you know you want it.
_comment_joinMode: "wish" (default) = the Guide's per-friend Join arms a join wish for the player's next search. "activation" = phase 2, the game's own join-a-friend launch. Leave "wish" unless you are testing phase 2.
_comment_mmStagePolicy: Where a seeker who picked a mission may be placed: "strict" (that mission or a lobby with none), "exact" (that mission only), "prefer"/"any" (any open lobby). Read again within ~2s of a change.
_comment_mmDropPlacedSeekerLobby: true = a seeker placed into someone else's lobby stops being a lobby others are placed into. false restores the old "ghost lobby" behaviour.
_comment_quietLogs: true = one short access line per request instead of the full request banner and per-request body dumps. Useful under load.
_comment_fastPaths: true = the same answers for less CPU (parse caches, compact JSON writes, config files checked every ~2s). Safe to leave on.
_comment_mmSkipFullLobbyPass: true = a host ticket from a lobby that cannot take anyone does not re-place every waiting seeker.
_comment_quietRoutineRequests: With quietLogs on: drop the access line for fast 2xx/304 responses and print one "[HTTP] last minute: ..." summary instead. 4xx/5xx and slow requests keep their line.
_comment_OTHER_FILES: Two more things the server reads that are NOT in this file and NOT in experimentalserver.py: (1) discord_app_id.txt next to experimentalserver.py - one line, the numeric Application ID of a Discord application YOU create at https://discord.com/developers/applications, handed to players so they get Rich Presence. Missing file = the Discord route answers null, which is fine. (2) data/_players.json - created and maintained by the server itself; it holds one random per-player login secret (secrets.token_hex(16)) generated at first sign-in. NEVER copy this file between servers and never share it: it is every player's password. It is not in source control and there is nothing to fill in by hand.
